hook: Trivial used to just mean where three roads meet.
modernAnchor: We use it to wave away anything unimportant, no roads involved.
journey: Latin trivium combined tri, three, and via, road, naming the spot where three roads met.
Crossroads were where ordinary people gathered, gossiped, and traded common, unremarkable news of the day.
Trivialis came to describe whatever belonged to that crossroads chatter, the kind everyone already knew.
English kept the word but dropped the roads, leaving only something too minor to matter.
